exceptions.reason: Action registries, validation, planning, and result handling are not implemented.
Agent address resolution, relationship storage, visibility, and provenance validation are not implemented.
Registry records, lifecycle transitions, and activation supervision are not implemented.
Artifact storage, admission, registry, and cache behavior are not implemented.
Atomic commit and outbox storage are not implemented.
Policy evaluation, attenuation, approvals, enforcement, and cache invalidation are not implemented.
Child directives, monitoring, cancellation, hard stop, and restart supervision are not implemented.
The implementation profile and diagnostic class registry are not implemented.
Threads, checkpoints, memory, approvals, quotas, custodians, leases, and receipts are not implemented.
Durable runtime and crash-injection infrastructure do not exist.
Fan-out scheduling, child work, durable aggregation, and integration fixtures are not implemented.
Guest SDKs, CLI, simulator, templates, fixtures, debug views, and reproducible build tooling are not implemented.
Directive validation, strategy snapshots, and terminal-state enforcement are not implemented.
Effect handlers, attempt leases, idempotency, and result ingress are not implemented.
Complete schema and semantic validation, canonical codecs, negative fixtures, and failure-atomicity evidence are not implemented.
Host-function registration, WASI policy, optimized instances, and residue testing are not implemented.
No guest SDK package or compiled conformance fixture corpus exists yet.
End-to-end host orchestration and Milestone 3 fixtures are not implemented.
Host operations, lifecycle, configuration, adapters, transports, and packaging are not implemented.
Canonical identity, version, diagnostic, and limit modules are not implemented.
Source adapters, schedule evaluation, timers, and ingress admission are not implemented.
The bootstrap Port adapter exists, but authorization, digest verification, complete resource limits, cancellation, output validation, and disposition evidence are not implemented.
Mailbox scheduling, overload policies, and turn leases are not implemented.
Model catalogs, bindings, request materialization, adapters, custody dispatch, streaming, and fixtures are not implemented.
Telemetry, audit, redaction, health, export, and operator-action systems are not implemented.
Strategy state machines, budgets, planning, loop detection, resume, and fixtures are not implemented.
Plugin registries, composition, configuration, approval, and lifecycle behavior are not implemented.
Production examples, runbooks, SLO measurement, evidence packages, and release acceptance do not exist.
Profile loading, enforcement, and publication are not implemented.
Signing, provenance, evidence storage, redaction, and security acceptance infrastructure are not implemented.
Durable retry, timers, replay, hibernation, and migration are not implemented.
Reducer orchestration and deterministic conformance fixtures are not implemented.
Signal schemas, routing, deduplication, and delivery tracking are not implemented.
Automated source-heading traceability and conflict gating are not implemented.
State-operation validation, patch application, and revision hashing are not implemented.
No durable storage adapter, snapshot store, or journal exists.
Principal authentication, trust assignment, grants, and threat controls are not implemented.
Tool catalog, retrieval, code sandbox, connector, custody, and result behavior are not implemented.
Topology versions, placement, activation leases, reconciliation, and fixtures are not implemented.
Multi-agent recovery, lease seams, and Milestone 6 acceptance fixtures are not implemented.
Agentic workflows and their integration acceptance corpus are not implemented.

requirements.statement: Reusable action descriptors shall declare schemas, state access, directive kinds, grants, determinism, and timeout independently of invocations.
Instructions and sequential or DAG plans shall validate before execution and use deterministic node ordering.
Results shall distinguish success, rejection, validation, infrastructure, diagnostics, patches, directives, and domain status.
External agent references shall use stable tenant-qualified logical addresses independent of process, engine, worker, socket, and node identity.
Relayed signals shall preserve validated origin, principal, correlation, causation, delegation chain, and return-address provenance within bounded depth.
Parent, child, owner, member, dependency, observer, delegate, and result-recipient relations shall enforce direction, consent, lifecycle, cardinality, and visibility.
Processes, Wasm instances, workers, sockets, and Port handles shall remain disposable and non-authoritative.
Create, resolve, activate, initialize, suspend, hibernate, thaw, cancel, complete, terminate, and inspect behavior shall enforce valid transitions.
The registry shall own tenant-scoped logical identity, artifact, lifecycle policy, revision, and activation state independently of live execution.
Admission shall apply the specified integrity, digest, signature, feature, manifest, schema, and policy checks before availability.
Artifacts shall be immutable content-addressed Wasm bundles whose manifest, schemas, modules, provenance, and cache identity are verified.
Manifests shall express logical model requirements without selecting providers, endpoints, connections, credentials, or custodians.
Ambiguous commit outcomes shall be resolved from durable revision, journal, and outbox identity without duplicate authoritative state.
No directive shall dispatch before its transition commits, and every outbox payload shall retain stable identity, hash, target, attempt, and state.
Snapshot, journal, directive outbox, and lifecycle changes shall commit as one compare-and-commit unit against the expected revision.
All populated restrictions shall combine restrictively, denials shall win, and authority shall never expand through fallback or substitution.
Host policy shall return allow, deny, approval-required, attenuated, or unavailable decisions with stable reasons for complete versioned inputs.
Policy shall be enforced at admission, action resolution, invocation, directive validation, effect dispatch, and result admission with revocation-safe caches.
Cancellation propagation, acknowledgement, hard stop, grant revocation, orphaning, and restart policy shall remain explicit and bounded.
Child admission shall atomically record logical identity, relationships, lifecycle policy, attenuated grants, journal intent, mailbox event, and evidence before activation.
Lifecycle events and monitor subscriptions shall be durable, ordered, replayable, bounded, and independent of live watch handles.
Invalid input, implementation-defined choices, presentation variation, limits, and runtime failures shall remain distinguishable observable classes.
Every claimed release shall publish supported versions, choices, options, deviations, limits, and bounded presentation variation.
Normative implementation work shall preserve the five canonical requirement words and their defined force.
Threads, messages, checkpoints, and working, episodic, semantic, and retrieved memory shall remain tenant-scoped projections with provenance, visibility, redaction, retention, and validation.
Credential leases shall authorize typed use only, keep handles and credentials non-exportable, require independent custodian checks, and verify correlated receipts before result admission.
Approval routing, decisions, expiry, escalation, quota reservation, consumption, release, windows, burst, and reconciliation shall be durable and policy controlled.
No directive from an uncommitted turn shall dispatch and every eligible committed directive shall retain a recoverable outbox record.
Fault tests shall retain a crash matrix for every specified commit, dispatch, acknowledgement, and result-ingress boundary.
Restart shall verify snapshots, replay journals, and restore outbox, timers, retries, hibernation, and migration state before normal work.
All, quorum, first-success, best-effort, and ordered aggregation shall be host-owned, deterministic, durable, and duplicate-aware.
Result conflicts, timeouts, cancellation, recovery, aggregation progress, and cross-milestone behavior shall retain bounded signed evidence.
Fan-out plans and work items shall use deterministic identities, bounded concurrency, deadlines, cancellation policy, attenuated grants, and result contracts.
Compatibility negotiation, deprecation, actionable failures, and capability-controlled redacted debug views shall remain versioned and testable.
Simulator controls, fixtures, templates, builds, and offline operation shall be isolated, reproducible, deterministic, and digest pinned.
Guest SDK and CLI surfaces shall preserve canonical host semantics for manifests, exports, codecs, artifacts, composition, fixtures, local execution, replay, reduction, and evidence inspection.
Emit, timer, effect, child-lifecycle, approval, and topology requests shall be represented as validated directives rather than guest-side effects.
Direct, FSM, and bounded-loop strategies shall use explicit serializable snapshots and logical model-slot references.
Completed and cancelled states shall reject ordinary continuation and preserve bounded diagnostics and evidence.
Every external dispatch shall use a durable leased attempt with stable request hash, outcome, timestamps, and retained evidence.
Dispatch shall validate handler registration, trust, capability, schema, idempotency, payload, duration, and result bounds.
Effect outcomes shall return as causally linked signals and shall not directly mutate an already committed reducer transition.
Protocol messages shall use validated canonical encoding with stable version, identity, revision, and diagnostic fields.
The bootstrap artifact shall expose describe, initialize, reduce, and migrate through the Extism no-argument bytes-in/bytes-out calling convention.
Decode, schema, semantic, revision, trap, timeout, cancellation, and limit failures shall publish no successful or partial authoritative result.
Each lifecycle export shall implement its specified request-response schema and semantic contract.
Synchronous host functions shall be deterministic, bounded, cancellable, retry-safe, typed, capability-gated, and tenant-aware.
Fresh, reset, pooled, and agent-pinned modes shall preserve memory, state, capability, resource, and residue isolation at least as strongly as fresh execution.
WASI shall be disabled by default and enabled only by an approved per-module request intersected with host policy.
SDK and Milestone 1 acceptance evidence shall retain fixture status, profile, versions, and unresolved variability.
Conformance shall be demonstrated by compiled guest artifacts and exact positive and negative fixtures rather than source-only tests.
Guest SDKs shall preserve protocol semantics while lowering language values, exports, codecs, signals, state operations, directives, strategies, and diagnostics.
Direct, FSM, timer, sensor, cancellation, and terminal flows shall retain complete bounded turn and regression evidence.
Trap, timeout, cancellation, invalid output, stale revision, and policy rejection shall leave no unauthorized successful or partial state.
A turn shall preserve the governing admission, dequeue, lease, snapshot, invocation, validation, commit, directive, and release order.
Transport, runtime, storage, telemetry, and secrets adapters plus packages shall preserve host semantics, compatibility, provenance, and bounded diagnostics.
Configure, initialize, ready, drain, shutdown, cancel, and health behavior shall validate layered configuration, profiles, secret references, and dependencies before readiness.
Embedded and server hosts shall expose the complete stable operation set through canonical request, response, error, pagination, idempotency, and streaming boundaries.
Tenant, principal, agent, artifact, invocation, signal, directive, attempt, and trace identities shall use their canonical stable representations and equality rules.
Version negotiation shall enforce compatible major, minor, and patch behavior with stable incompatibility diagnostics.
Resource-limit exhaustion shall be distinct from malformed input and shall disclose the applicable configured limit safely.
Schedule timezone, misfire, and jitter behavior shall be validated and deterministic for a schedule and fire time.
Timer identities shall be tenant scoped and timer signals shall not be admitted before their absolute due time.
User, transport, sensor, schedule, and timer events shall pass authentication, resolution, schema validation, deduplication, and mailbox admission.
Success, trap, timeout, cancellation, and invalid output shall dispose or quarantine the instance with bounded evidence.
The host shall verify tenant authorization and artifact digest before creating a fresh bounded guest instance for each turn.
Guest output shall pass byte, encoding, schema, patch, revision, directive-capability, and usage checks before state logic observes it.
A valid per-agent lease and current fencing token shall be required for a turn, renewal, and authoritative completion.
Mailboxes shall enforce priority, FIFO tie behavior, fairness, count, byte, age, source, tenant, and delivery bounds.
Overload shall produce the configured reject, defer, coalesce, supersede, or dead-letter outcome with stable diagnostics.
Agents shall emit provider-neutral model intents while users own versioned concrete connection, provider, model, and custodian bindings outside artifacts.
The host shall atomically materialize and pin request identity, binding revision, provider, model, digest, budget, quota, outbox, and idempotency across retry and replay.
Streaming, final response, usage, cancellation, credential use, and receipt admission shall remain bounded, normalized, tenant-safe, and credential-free.
Metrics, traces, structured logs, and audit records shall use bounded versioned schemas, causal correlation, controlled cardinality, retention, export, and tenant authorization.
Drain, pause, resume, retry, cancel, quarantine, reconcile, rotate, and inspect actions shall be authorized, audited, idempotent, bounded, and safely observable.
Sensitive data shall be redacted before exposure, and liveness, readiness, dependencies, runtime profile, queue, storage, scheduler, and coordinator health shall remain accurate and bounded.
The current Elixir package shall compile and pass its ExUnit suite.
The package shall not claim implemented conformance until applicable exceptions are replaced by linked or executed evidence and normative acceptance gates pass.
Agent WASM shall be delivered as an Elixir/OTP product whose public programming and operations surfaces belong to the Mix application.
Package behavior shall follow the complete applicable normative source corpus and shall not use implementation behavior to resolve source conflicts silently.
The SpecLed workspace shall maintain one implementation subject for each of the 39 numbered technical areas and two governance specifications.
Turn, token, tool, cost, time, iteration, and recursion limits plus loop, repeated-request, contradiction, missing-result, and model-drift detection shall force explicit termination.
Direct, FSM, tool-loop, and planning strategies shall use explicit serialized state, plans, waits, iterations, budgets, and bounded history without hidden continuation.
Snapshot migration, deterministic resume, plan adaptation, state transitions, and every failure class shall retain bounded evidence and integration proof.
Composition shall use deterministic plugin ordering and reject name, route, namespace, schema, migration, capability, and lifecycle conflicts atomically.
Install, validate, configure, approve, enable, disable, upgrade, migrate, rollback, and remove shall preserve user bindings, trust, and review gates.
Plugin manifests shall declare immutable artifacts, actions, routes, namespaces, schemas, strategies, logical requirements, grants, and lifecycle ownership.

Canonical examples and dependency, overload, stuck-turn, repeated-effect, divergence, revocation, tenant-incident, recovery, and rollback runbooks shall use supported surfaces and reproducible evidence.
Conformance, security, performance, runbook, example, support-matrix, residual-risk, ownership, deployment, and verification evidence shall gate production release.
Admission, latency, durability, effect delay, recovery, availability, isolation, and evidence completeness shall have measured objectives, budgets, alerts, immutable evidence, and retained reports.
The bootstrap guest profile shall expose the portable reducer boundary without ambient WASI or credential authority.
A release shall publish its supported profile, versions, extensions, choices, and limits.
Profiles shall preserve host authority over identity, state, scheduling, policy, effects, topology, and evidence while guests remain deterministic proposal producers.
Threat-to-control, malicious-input, tenant-isolation, revocation, residue, and audit-tampering exercises shall gate security acceptance.
Artifact admission shall verify digest, signature, publisher, build provenance, dependencies, toolchain compatibility, and revocation before availability.
Security and authority events shall produce immutable tamper-evident host-owned evidence before dependent actions proceed.
Retry and timer records shall be durable, bounded, independently recoverable, and classified for transient, permanent, or operator intervention outcomes.
Migration shall require authorization, compatible path, checkpoint, rollback state, atomic audit evidence, and safe failure behavior.
Replay shall reconstruct pinned history without external effects, and hibernation shall deactivate only after verified snapshot and checkpoint durability.
Replay and metamorphic fixtures shall prove field-order and canonical-reencoding equivalence and reject stale or unauthorized output.
Identical canonical inputs and profile shall produce canonically equivalent outputs without ambient nondeterminism.
Reducer resolution shall preserve the specified signal, routing, execution, patch, directive, and result-construction order.
The host shall authenticate, authorize, validate, deduplicate, and deterministically route signals before delivery.
Accepted, rejected, deferred, delivered, redelivered, coalesced, and dead-lettered outcomes shall remain explicit and bounded.
Signals shall be immutable tenant-scoped envelopes with stable source, subject, correlation, causation, delivery, trace, and timestamp data.
Conflicting normative rules, ambiguity, and normative silence shall block conformance for the disputed behavior.
Implementation behavior and conformance claims shall follow applicable normative specification chapters and visibly normative content.
Tests, implementation, and evidence shall cite governing document headings and shall not override normative text.
Set, delete, merge, append, increment, and test operations shall apply in order and atomically against an expected base revision.
Stale revisions, failed preconditions, invalid paths, schema violations, and patch limits shall reject the patch without partial state.
Successful state changes shall produce monotonic hash-linked revisions from canonical state.
Storage adapters shall provide isolated reads, serializable compare-and-commit writes, durability, conflict rejection, backup, and recovery.
Audit and reconstruction journals shall be append-only, ordered, atomic, and sufficient for reconstruction while conversation views remain filtered projections.
Durable snapshots shall be tenant isolated, revisioned, checksummed, lifecycle consistent, and verified on every read.
Security controls shall address the specified malicious guests, compromised components, confused deputies, tenants, dependencies, operators, co-tenants, and host threats.
Grants shall independently bind principal, tenant, capability, resource, purpose, operation, constraints, expiry, and delegation without ambient authority.
Authentication shall bind the closed principal kinds and assign trust only through provenance, authorization, and tenant isolation.
Tool descriptors and catalog queries shall validate schemas, provenance, capability, side-effect class, tenant scope, status, timeout, and result limits.
Authenticated connector operations shall use user-owned bindings, independent credential-use authority, typed custodian dispatch, receipt verification, and direct-egress denial.
Retrieval, code, and tool operations shall execute through bounded durable attempts with tenant isolation, provenance, cancellation, and normalized result signals.
Desired topology shall be durable and immutable per version, observed status shall be durable, and live placement shall remain disposable.
Placement authority shall require unexpired activation leases and monotonic fencing that rejects stale hosts.
Reconciliation shall process missing, extra, failed, stale, moved, incompatible, and dependency-blocked nodes in the governing order with evidence.
Restart shall distrust pre-restart live placement and reconstruct bounded live agents from verified durable topology and observed status.
Recovery and topology shall not create cross-tenant routes, relationships, grants, results, mailboxes, leases, or placement authority.
Horizontal lease transfer, topology distribution, and reconciliation coordination shall remain versioned replaceable seams with bounded evidence.
Workflow, provenance, safety, cost, resume, credential non-exposure, and residual model-risk evidence shall gate Milestone 7 acceptance.
Direct model, structured response, model-tool continuation, retrieval-grounded, code-execution, and multi-agent workflows shall use durable explicit state and pinned dependencies.
Hostile output, approvals, quotas, credential revocation, stream cancellation, provenance, and workflow budgets shall be validated before state, context, tool, or user admission.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that tells agents to start a session with mix spec.prime before editing current truth.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
When indexing and validation run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state.
